string.text: The GSh-18 is a 9x19mm semi-automatic pistol developed in the early 1990s at the KBP Instrument Design Bureau in Tula. The pistol's name is derived from its designers - Gryazev and Shipunow, and the number 18 denotes the magazine capacity. The GSh-18 is a recoil-operated, locked breech pistol. The weapon has an unusual cam-rotated barrel with 10 locking lugs. The GSh-18 is striker fired and features a pre-set trigger that pre-cocks the pistol when the slide recoils after firing a shot, the striker firing pin is then fully cocked by pulling the trigger back to the rear. With the 7N21 and 7N31 armour-piercing bullets, it can pierce 8mm of steel at 20 metres.

The UMP was developed by H&K in the 1990s, first appearing on the market in 1999. The idea behind the UMP was to create lightweight and powerful submachine gun, that was also cheaper than the MP5. The UMP, being targeted primarily for US law enforcement, appeared in .45ACP and .40SW chamberings, and later in 9mm. Providing greater stopping power than the MP5, the UMP45 also produces more recoil. This makes controlling full automatic fire more difficult. The UMP45's cyclic rate of fire was lowered significantly to combat this problem.

The 92F is perhaps best known as the standard pistol of the US Military, replacing the legendary M1911. It is a short-recoil operated, locked-breech weapon with an aluminium frame and a hard chromed barrel bore. A popular sidearm adopted by several countries, it is especially popular among criminals for its high-powered rounds and high-capacity magazine.

The TT-33 is a Russian 7.62x25mm pistol. It was developed in the early 1930s by Fedor Tokarev as a service pistol for the Soviet military to replace the Nagant M1895 revolver. Many communist or Soviet bloc countries made a variation of the TT-33 pistol, until it was eventually replaced by 9x18mm Makarov PM in 1952. Production of the TT-33 in the USSR ended in 1954.

The 92F is perhaps best known as the standard pistol of the US Military, replacing the legendary M1911. It is a short-recoil operated, locked-breech weapon with an aluminium frame and a hard chromed barrel bore. A popular sidearm adopted by several countries, it is especially popular among criminals for its high-powered rounds and high-capacity magazine.

The Px4 Storm is an advancement of the Beretta 8000, meant to be as a replacer of the 92FS for personal defense and law enforcement use. Its rotating barrel allows for better recoil control and continuous shots, the lightframe also helps with the weight. This particular model seems to come with tritium sights as well. From the looks of it, these weapons were "illegally" exported from Armenia and Romania, by mercenaries that used to be part of the police force from said countries.

Intended for professional and amateur hunting the TOZ-34 is an over/under shotgun. Though lacking in capacity, only 2 rounds, it compares well with high-grade shotguns due to its high accuracy of hits. The TOZ 34 was designed by N. I. Korovyakov and V. P. Ochnev in 1965. Affordable in price, with high damage output and its ability to unload both rounds instantly make it a popular weapon among rookies on the outskirts of the Zone. Especially useful against mutants thanks to its accuracy and stopping power.

Intended for professional and amateur hunting the TOZ-34 is an over/under shotgun. Though lacking in capacity, only 2 rounds, it compares well with high-grade shotguns due to its high accuracy of hits. The TOZ 34 was designed by N. I. Korovyakov and V. P. Ochnev in 1965. Affordable in price, with high damage output and its ability to unload both rounds instantly make it a popular weapon among rookies on the outskirts of the Zone. Especially useful against mutants thanks to its accuracy and stopping power. This model has a Leupold Mark 4 scope attached to it.

Intended for professional and amateur hunting the TOZ-34 is a over/under shotgun. Modifications made to this gun by removing much of the barrel and the stock makes this shotgun more compact and easier to carry. Popular among rookies and bandits as they can hide it easily in their trench coats.

Developed by the American company Magnum Research, the Desert Eagle uses a gas operated mechanism commonly found in rifles. This allows the pistol to use much larger caliber bullets than traditional semi-automatic pistols. The disadvantages of this weapon include a considerable size and heavy weight. On this barrel, all components are perfectly tuned to achieve the highest accuracy for pistols of this type, thanks to the integrated muzzle compensator, it was possible to significantly reduce recoil. It has a heavily redesigned picatinny rail, thanks to which a wide range of scopes can be mounted. This weapon was brought to the Zone by stalker Logan Williams. Under the guise of a journalist-photographer, he managed to reach the center of Pripyat alone. Currently, his fate is unknown, but there are rumors that he works as an informant for many secret departments on the Exclusion Zone.

Developed by the American company Magnum Research, the Desert Eagle uses a gas operated mechanism commonly found in rifles. This allows the pistol to use much larger caliber bullets than traditional semi-automatic pistols. The disadvantages of this weapon include a considerable size and heavy weight.

The SPAS-12 is a dual-mode shotgun, designed for combat and anti-riot measures. It is employed by many special military and police units around the world. With its distinctive heat shield and folding stock, the SPAS-12 is an iconic firearm. Notable for its reliability and tactical flexibility. Despite its heavy weight, complex mechanism and considerable cost, it is in demand in the Zone due to its effectiveness against mutants.

The Fort-17 pistol is the latest development of the Ukrainian state owned FORT factory. It is a polymer framed modification of the earlier Fort-12 pistol, and all the mechanisms and properties are almost identical between the two pistols. However, the Fort-17 is lighter than its predecessor and features a removable grip backstrap, which can be had in various sizes, to adapt the pistol for a particular shooter.

The FN P90 submachine gun was developed in the late 1980s as a personal defence weapon for troops whose primary activities does not include small arms, such as vehicle and tank crew members, artillery crews etc. Standard pistols and submachine guns were proven ineffective against enemies wearing body armour. FN designers developed a new round, initially designated as SS90, to achieve high penetration while keeping recoil low FN used a small-bore approach, creating a round that looked like the scaled down 5.56 NATO round. The result was FN P90 personal defence weapon, introduced in 1990 along with improved 5.7x28 SS190 ammunition which replaced polymer cored bullets with heavier dual core, steel and aluminium, bullets for better penetration against body armour.

The MP5 is one of the most famous and wide spread firearms of its class. The MP5's compactness, accuracy and reliability have made it a favourite of numerous military, law enforcement, intelligence and security organisations the world over. The MP5A3 is fitted with a retractable metal stock. Not surprisingly, having flooded the global black markets, it eventually made its way to the Zone.
A submachine gun prototype based on the excellent H&K MP5A3 model. Designed as a next generation close quarter combat weapon, it benefits from a higher calibre, rate of fire and accuracy.
A variant of the MP5 with an integrated suppressor. In the Zone, mercenaries prefer this variant to the normal one.

The Mosin-Nagant is a legendary bolt action rifle that dates back to the 19th century, having seen use in both World Wars. While no longer in military service, its cheap price makes it the first rifle for many civilians.
The PU is a 3.5x scope designed in 1940 for the Mosin-Nagant rifle.

A crude knife of handicraft production, made by some craftsman. Quickly enough, it becomes unusable due to the bad quality and poor combat performance, especially for stabbing. Nevertheless, it is the most common type of knives used in the Zone for being very cheap. It meets the needs of most stalkers. \n \n %c[255, 220, 53, 69] � %c[255, 220, 53, 69] unsuitable for chopping thick-skinned mutants

A large hunting knife with a rugged rubber handle. Sharp and well maintained. It might not be good at penetrating combat armors but due to the toothed blade it is ideal at causing massive, bleeding wounds to open flesh. This is makes it a perfect choice when confronting animals, especially when finishing off already wounded ones.\n \n %c[255, 220, 53, 69] � %c[255, 220, 53, 69] unsuitable for chopping thick-skinned mutants

Practical knife with a wide range of applications, from sharpening sticks to cutting meat and thick hides of large mutants like wild boars. It is a preferable choice among stalkers due to its versatility and reliability, more experienced stalkers however prefer high-quality combat knives. Combat characteristics are not remarkable, but with proper skill and experience it can deal significant damage to the target.

A very durable hunting knife with a large blade of stainless steel. Ideal for handling larger animals, meat and thick hides. It is able to cause massive, bleeding wounds. Its draw-back is that it does not pierce heavy armors with adequate effectiveness.

Combat knife is designed for special operations. Modern designs are versatile at low weight. The sharpness and shape of the blade allow you to cut the ropes with ease, open cans and punch standard army bulletproof vests. These knives have a very high value in the range of FDS because of its efficiency and small distribution. It's a desirable acquisition for any Stalker.
Box with 7.62x51 cartridge belts for the M60 machine gun.
Pistol cartridge with a bullet of large caliber for the Desert Eagle pistol.
American revolver cartridge of remarkably high power.
Soviet pistol cartridge of 7.62 mm for pistol TT-33 and submachine guns PPSH-41 and PPS-41. Simple all-metal bullet.
Soviet pistol cartridge of 7.62 mm for pistol TT-33 and submachine guns PPSH-41 and PPS-41. Improved armor-piercing variant with steel core and copper jacket.
A wonderful means of annihilating enemies at a distance. Shooting at it creates a mini-apocalypse within an 8 meter radius.
American revolver cartridge of high power.

00 buckshot is one of the most common 12 gauge rounds, typically used for self-defense. It features nine pellets that are about .33 inches in diameter each, and have good stopping power at close range. Limited effectiveness against bulletproof armor.
These are standard 1 oz lead slug rounds for 12 gauge shotguns, one of the most common types of round. Effective against human and monster alike, although not the most effective at penetrating armor.
These slug rounds are rifled to improve accuracy, and feature a hardened steel core that can more effectively penetrate armor than regular 12 gauge slugs.

The 12.7 x 55 mm round is used in some Russian firearms, such as the VKS sniper rifle and the SzAK-12 combat rifle and the RSz-12 revolver. The cartridge can carry a projectile weighing from 108 to 1173 grains and is primarily used for firing heavy subsonic charges. A high-penetration VKS round can penetrate up to 16 mm (0.63 in) of steel per 200 meters (220 km) or armor up to GOST 5 or NIJ III per 100 meters (110 km). The accuracy of this cartridge, when loaded with precision VKS rounds, is to be one MOA per 100 meters (110 yards) up to the effective range limit of 600 meters (660 yards). Despite the same caliber, the SzAK-12 (and RSz-12) would not be able to feed or charge ammunition designed for VKS due to the significant length differences in the projectile component and thus require its own shorter payloads. The SzAK-12 rounds have a shorter range compared to the VKS, and the maximum effective range of the charges ranges from 100 to 300 meters (110 to 330 yards).

This 12.7 x 55mm round is used in some Russian firearms, such as the VKS sniper rifle and the SzAK-12 combat rifle and the RSz-12 revolver. A high-penetration VKS projectile can penetrate up to 16 mm (0.63 in) of steel per 200 meters (220 km) or armor up to GOST 5 or NIJ III per 100 meters (110 km). The accuracy of this round, when loaded with precision VKS rounds, is to be one MOA per 100 meters (110 yards) up to the effective range limit of 600 meters (660 yards). Despite the same caliber, the SzAK-12 (and RSz-12) would not be able to feed or charge ammunition designed for VKS due to the significant length differences in the projectile component and thus require its own shorter payloads. The SzAK-12 missiles have a shorter range compared to the VKS, and the maximum effective range of the charges ranges from 100 to 300 meters (110 to 330 yards). The VPS variety differs from the variety by increased penetration.
Standard issue 9x18 mm Makarov pistol rounds. These have been in service since the 1950s. Stopping power is rather low and it is ineffective against armor.
These 9x18 mm rounds feature a hardened steel core designed to improve its effectiveness against armor.
Standard issue 9x19 mm Parabellum rounds, one of the most common pistol cartridges in the world. Similar in performance to 9x18 mm, these rounds are ineffective against armor.

+P+ designates a highly pressurized round. These 9x19 mm rounds produce higher muzzle velocity and thus greater kinetic impact and stopping power. However, they have more recoil and produce slightly more wear on the gun.

5.7x28 mm rounds are a fairly modern development by FN Herstal. They are very small pistol/submachine gun rounds, however they produce among the highest muzzle velocity of any pistol round and are more effective against armor than most. Designed exclusively for the FN P90 and FN Five-Seven.
These 5.7x28 mm rounds feature a Jacketed Hollow Point bullet that expands upon impact. It has much less penetration than the standard SS190 round, but greater stopping power.

.50 Action Express (AE) rounds are extremely powerful, high recoil magnum pistol rounds designed for the Desert Eagle pistol. Effective for big game hunting, .50 AE pistols are favored by wealthier stalkers who make a living hunting large mutants.

Standard .357 magnum FMJ rounds. These have been around since the 1930s and are still in use today due to their undeniable effectiveness. They feature tremendous stopping power but remain controllable even when fired out of a revolver.

Standard issue .45ACP (Automatic Colt Pistol) designed for NATO pistols and submachine guns. This is a subsonic round that can thus be more effectively suppressed. Improved stopping power over standard 9mm cartridges.

.45ACP (Automatic Colt Pistol) Hydra-Shock rounds feature a Jacketed Hollow Point bullet that expands upon impact, greatly reducing its penetration but creating much deadlier wound channels in tissue.

7N10 rounds are considered "improved penetration" cartridges for AK-74 type rifles. They were created in 1992 to replace cartridges such as 7N6M. Modern body armors can still effectively stop these rounds, however.

7N22 designates armor-piercing 5.45x39 mm cartridges designed for AK-74 type rifles. They feature a sharp-pointed steel penetrator made of steel U12A and retains the soft lead plug in the nose for jacket discarding.
Standard issue Belgian made 5.56x45 mm NATO rifle rounds. While they are capable of decent accuracy and range, they are notoriously ineffective against body armor and are lacking in stopping power.
These 5.56x45 mm rounds feature an improved armor-piercing core compared to SS109. Designed for NATO rifles such as the AR-15 platform, HK G36, and many others.

SP-5 designates match grade ammunition. These are subsonic rounds offering improved accuracy. They are ideal for stealth engagements within 200 meters thanks to their subsonic design, which does not produce an audible sound signature characteristic of supersonic bullets. When combined with a silenced firearm, this round is perfect for close-range assassination.

PAB-9 rounds are a cheap alternative to 9x39 mm SP-6. Their accuracy is thus inferior. Generally speaking, 9x39 mm rounds are subsonic and thus more easily suppressed, somewhat effective against body armor, and have limited effective range of around 200 meters.

SP-6 is the designation for armor-piercing 9x39 mm rounds. These are subsonic rounds that are more easily suppressed and do not produce a loud noise signature. When combined with a silenced weapon, they allow for discreet engagements without revealing the shooter's position. Their ideal use is for assassinations at around 200 meters distance or less.

The 7.62x25 mm Tokarev round saw extensive use during WWII. It is no longer used in modern weaponry, but compared to 9x18 mm Makarov, it provides increased stopping power and penetration. Used in the Tokarev TT pistol and PPSh submachine guns.
These 7.62x25 mm rounds have a hardened steel core for improved effectiveness against armor. Used in the Tokarev TT pistol and PPSh submachine guns.

The 7.62x39 mm round was first used in the AK-47. 57-N-231 designates a standard infantry grade steel core bullet. This round has deadly stopping power and good penetration, but poor accuracy and limited effective range.

The 7.62x39 mm round was first used in the AK-47. 7N23 designates an improved armor-piercing round. This round has deadly stopping power and good penetration, but poor accuracy and limited effective range.

Standard issue 7.62x51 mm NATO rounds with a full metal jacketed bullet. This is a multipurpose .30 caliber round for NATO battle rifles, sniper rifles, and machine guns. High stopping power and good penetration.
Older armor-piercing 7.62x51 mm NATO round. This is a multipurpose .30 caliber round for NATO battle rifles, sniper rifles, and machine guns. High stopping power and improved penetration.

The 7.62x54mmR cartridge dates back to the late 19th century. It has been used in long range rifles and machine guns ever since. 7N1 designates a sniper round, for use with the likes of the Dragunov SVD, SVU, and SV-98 rifles.

The 7.62x54mmR cartridge dates back to the late 19th century. It has been used in long range rifles and machine guns ever since. 7N14 designates an improved match grade sniper round with an armor piercing steel core bullet.
The 7.62x54mmR cartridge dates back to the late 19th century. It has been used in long range rifles and machine guns ever since. 7N26 (previously 7N13) designates an improved armor piercing round.

Standard issue 7.92x57 mm Mauser round that dates back to the start of the 20th century. Used during both World Wars, this is a very large and powerful round, but lacks the accuracy of newer and improved .30 caliber rounds.

Higher quality 7.92x57 mm Mauser round with an improved armor-piercing core. This round dates back to the start of the 20th century. Used during both World Wars, this is a very large and powerful round, but lacks the accuracy of newer and improved .30 caliber rounds.

.338 Lapua Magnum rounds were designed to be the ultimate sniper round. They are capable of accurate fire at extremely long distances, with a maximum range that exceeds 2 km. The penetration and stopping power of these rounds is tremendous.

The 12.7x55 mm cartridge is a massive subsonic bullet of Russian origin. This is a rarely used round that features high recoil, high stopping power, and deadly armor penetration capability, but has limited range.

The .50 Browning Machine Gun cartridge entered official service in 1921 for anti-materiel and heavy machine gun use, but it is also a very effective sniper round. The M1022 designation is for long range sniper rounds and training, and it lacks any enhanced armor piercing or other effects.
High tech ammunition for the Gauss Rifle. Consists of a 2mm capsule and is powered by fragments of the Flash artifact.
Lower quality ammunition for the Gauss Rifle produced by Cardan.
This is a box of 7.62x54mmR tracer ammunition meant for machine guns. Not well suited for sniper use.
The OG-7V is an anti-personnel fragmentation rocket for the RPG-7. It is not designed to be used against armored vehicles.

The F1 grenade is a Soviet anti-personnel fragmentation defensive grenade. It has a steel exterior that is notched to facilitate fragmentation upon detonation and to prevent hands from slipping. It features 60g of TNT and has a 3.5-4 second fuse. The radius of the shrapnel dispersion is up to 200 meters (effective radius is about 30 meters).
The RGD-5 hand grenade is a Soviet era fragmentation grenade. It has a 110g TNT explosive charge and produces about 350 fragments upon detonation. It has a 3.2 - 4.2 second fuse.
This grenade produces a smoke screen to cover infantry movements, most effective within the first 10 seconds of detonation.

Chemical lighting grenade. Designed to illuminate areas during low light and low visibility conditions, as well as for blinding and disorientation of the enemy during combat engagements. The duration is less than a minute.
40mm high explosive grenade designed for the GP series grenade launchers. Contains 48g of A-IX-1 explosive.

This is a special 40mm grenade for GP series grenade launchers. On impact, a small charge in the nose of the grenade is detonated; this raises the grenade 0.5 to 1.5m in the air, before an impact delay fuse detonates it. Contains 37g of TNT explosive and has a lethal radius of about 6 meters.
40mm high explosive grenade designed for the M203 grenade launcher. Most effective against grouped infantry formations.
